question.text: The volcanoes Mount Pinatubo (pin-uh-TOO-boh) and Mount Mayon (mah-YAWN) are located on this island, the largest in the Philippines.
question.clue: This island, which sits to the south of the Babuyan Islands, is also home to the basin of the Cagayan River and Clark Air Base, which was heavily damaged by another of its volcanoes.

swap.leadin: One photograph taken in this country shows a naked girl covered in napalm screaming and running towards the viewer.
swap.text: Name this country, where the United States was engaged in a controversial war in the 1960s and 1970s. Another photograph taken here by Eddie Adams depicts a police chief shooting a plaid-shirted rebel.
swap.clue: Rioting against the presence of one of these countries in the other resulted in a coup which created the government in exile GRUNK.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Asian political families.
question.text: One member of this family dealt with the aftermath of Typhoon Haiyan in 2013. His mother Corazon's controversial 1986 election loss led to the People Power Revolution.
question.clue: A member of this family, who was supported by Cardinal Sin, founded the Lakas ng Bayan Party and was assassinated at an airport which now bears his name.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Marshal Phibun.
swap.text: After a 1932 coup in which Phibun came to power in this country governed from Bangkok, he changed its official name from Siam to a name meaning "land of the free."
swap.clue: The TRT party of Thaksin Shinawatra was deposed in a 2006 coup in this country where strong lese-majeste laws protected the popularity of its long-lived king Bhumibol.

question.leadin: During this battle, the artillery commander Charles Piroth blew himself up with a hand grenade after falsely claiming that the Viet Minh would not be able to use their artillery successfully.
question.text: Name this 1954 battle in which the Viet Minh decisively defeated French colonial forces, putting an end to the First Indochina War.
question.clue: At this battle the defending troops were commanded by Colonel Christian de Castries and it ended the day before the Geneva Accords were signed.

swap.text: Viet Minh forces during the battle were led by this man, who later commanded the People's Army of Vietnam during the Vietnam War.
swap.clue: The Viet Minh at Dien Bien Phu were led by this master general, who would later oppose U.S. troops during the Tet Offensive.

question.leadin: The Thirtieth of September Movement was an attempted coup against this leader.
question.text: Name this leader who established a system of "Guided Democracy." This first president of Indonesia hosted the Bandung conference, which eventually led to the development of the Non-Aligned Movement.
question.clue: This leader hosted the meeting which led to the formation of the Non-Aligned Movement in his country's city of Bandung.

swap.leadin: Kosa Pan led an embassy sent by this kingdom to the French court.
swap.text: Name this Siamese kingdom. The Greek adventurer Constantine Phaulkon served as an adviser to this kingdom's ruler Narai the Great.
swap.answerHtml: Ayutthaya Kingdom [prompt on, but do not otherwise reveal Thailand]
swap.clue: Under its King Naresuan, this dynasty defeated an Eastern invader at the Battle of Nong Sarai.

question.text: This ruler was unable to conquer Dai-Viet, but did sack the Champa capital Vijaya. He is best known, however, for the creation of Beng Mealea and another complex dedicated to Vishnu. For 15 points, identify this ruler of the Khmer Empire, who oversaw the construction of Ankgor Wat.
question.clue: The Khmer built the world's largest religious complex at Angkor Wat under this ruler, who is depicted in massive stone heads around the building. This ruler befriended the Chola Dynasty.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Asian dynasties.
swap.text: This general of king Taksin took the throne of Siam in 1782 and became the founder of the Chakkri dynasty. All subsequent kings of Thailand have shared his name.

question.leadin: In this modern-day country, the badass Naresuan [nah-ray-SOO-un] was a leader of the Ayutthaya [ah-YOO-tee-ah] Kingdom.
question.text: Name this Southeast Asian country that was ruled by war criminal and former Manchester City owner Thaksin Shinawatra.
question.clue: Its rulers used the Paknam Incident to create an irredentist nationalism later deployed by the Phibun government.

swap.leadin: The death of a monarch with this name was initially ruled an accident despite shots to his back.
swap.text: Give this regnal name of Ananda Mahidol, whose predecessor was criticized during a 1932 constitutional revolution. All rulers of the Rattanakosin ("rat-tan-uh-KOH-sin") kingdom took on this regnal name.
swap.clue: The first king of this name ascended to the position after executing his predecessor, King Taksin, while the fourth ruler of this name died of malaria after watching a solar eclipse he had predicted.

question.text: Excessive taxation imposed under the Toungoo ("TOWN-goo") dynasty in this modern-day country transformed its Irrawaddy delta region into what one historian termed a "depopulated desert."
question.answerHtml: Myanmar [or Republic of the Union of Myanmar; accept Burma]
question.clue: One disastrous scheme in this country involved denominating currency in base 9 rather than base 10, while a wave of protests in this country following the death of a UN secretary general were named for the date on which they took place, August 8, 1988.

swap.text: General Harold Briggs approved the use of this chemical to destroy jungles during the Malayan Emergency. It was more famously used in the Vietnam War.
swap.clue: This carcinogen and defoliant that the United States used in an attempt to increase the visibility of Viet Cong troops.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the 30th of September Movement, whose most significant action, the murder of six generals, actually took place on October 1st, 1965.
question.text: The military blamed this political party for the murders, using the 30th of September Movement as a pretext for the mass murder of its members. This party was subsequently banned in March 1966, and remains illegal today.
question.clue: This party was exonerated of responsibility for a coup attempt in the "Cornell Paper" written by Benedict Anderson and Ruth McVey.

swap.leadin: Some of the most vicious combat in this campaign was seen during the engagement known as the Battle of the Tennis Court.
swap.text: Name this theatre of the Second World War where Operation U-Go was halted in two fierce battles in 1944 when infiltration tactics and encirclement were rendered ineffective by air supply to the defenders, while many of the attacking force's 50,000-plus casualties were caused by malnutrition and malaria.

question.leadin: Along with purchasing the superyacht Equanimity, funds embezzled in this scandal were ironically used to finance Red Granite Pictures's production of The Wolf of Wall Street.
question.text: Name this scandal in which president Najib Razak and his conspirators siphoned billions from Malaysia's sovereign wealth fund.

swap.leadin: A ruler from this family often held court with his pet orangutan Betsy, and he once held a trial in which he sentenced a man-eating crocodile to "be instantly killed without honours."
swap.text: Name this royal family, whose rule began when Omar Ali Saifuddin II granted its patriarch territory around the modern-day city of Kuching and the region of Bau. As rulers, they were known as the "White Rajahs."

question.text: This monk's self-immolation, an act of protest against Diem, was captured by Malcolm Browne. In that picture, this man sits still in front of a car with its hood popped open as he burnt to death.

swap.text: This Indonesian diplomat organized the Bandung Convention, and later served as ambassador to the United Nations under Suharto.
